summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with multiple sclerosis, neurogenic bladder, and a chronic indwelling Foley catheter, was admitted for weakness and fever. He was diagnosed with Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteremia and a urinary tract infection, likely originating from his catheter and a bladder stone. His creatinine was elevated on admission due to dehydration, which resolved with IV fluids. A PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic therapy, and he underwent surgical lithotripsy to remove the infected bladder stone. Blood cultures cleared, and his white count normalized. He was discharged to an extended care facility to complete a 6-day course of IV cefepime, with plans for weekly Foley catheter changes and initiation of methenamine and vitamin C for UTI suppression. Follow-up with infectious disease was arranged.
problems: Infection and inflammatory reaction due to indwelling urinary catheter
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
